issue.title: HttpClientRequest sends headers with lower case key and out of order.

labels.name: area-core-library
labels.description: SDK core library issues (core, async, ...); use area-vm or area-web for platform specific libraries.

issue.body_html:
The server requires the http headers to be ordered and case-sensitive, but Dart cannot do this.

For example, in the following code, the key of the request headers received by the server is all lowercase, and the order is also disrupted(possibly {'b ':'b', 'd': 'd', 'c': 'c', 'a': 'a',}).

    final client = HttpClient();
    final request = await client.getUrl(Uri.parse(url));
    final headers = {
      'A': 'a',
      'B': 'b',
      'C': 'c',
      'D': 'd',
    };
    headers.forEach((key, value) {
      request.headers.set(key, value);
    });

comments.body:
> The server requires the http headers to be ordered and case-sensitive, but Dart cannot do this.

That's the bug in the server. Refer to HTTP/1.1 specification. RFC 2616 section 4.2 Message Headers says:

> Field names are case-insensitive.
> [...]
> The order in which header fields with differing field names are received is not significant.

I don't know if supporting non-compliant servers which don't follow RFC 2616 is a goal or not for our builtin client. 

I defer to @brianquinlan to make the call.

comments.body:
If we can allow people to control the header precisely, even if it requires going through a more cumbersome API than the default, I think it is a reasonable feature.

You may want to build specific headers to test your server code, and not only test it with the headers that `dart:io` sends by default.

It'd also be reasonable to defer to a secondary library for something like that, like `package:http` or a new `package:custom_http` (or whatever, naming is hard). It doesn't have to be part of the default implementation unless those other packages need it. 

The big question then becomes who should implement it, and what priority it deserves.
